reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the cited paragraphs contain no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right binding the Customer; §6 is a one-way transparency provision in our favour and §3(e) gives Client access to its own usage data.

Absence of any Vendor audit right leaves us better off than the preferred position, so treating it as compliant (rather than 'missing') is correct for this protective rule — inserting audit machinery would create an obligation against us and would be over-flagging.
No redline and no counterparty comment were produced, which is the expected output for a compliant finding; the original and rendered paragraphs are identical.
The failed deterministic check ('audit frequency limited') is explained by the total absence of an audit clause rather than by a defective clause, so it does not undermine the verdict.
§8(f) is correctly characterised as vendor self-help on its own Interface, not remote access to or audit of Client systems, so it does not trigger the walk-away condition.
